sapience_notes.subject: git %an is mailmap-blind; only %aN and %aE honour .mailmap
sapience_notes.value: On git 2.54.0, `git log --format='%an'` ignores .mailmap entirely and `--use-mailmap` does not rescue it; only the capital-letter placeholders %aN/%aE are folded. Measured on a 17831-commit repository: a header-attribution check reading %aN reports 27 candidates out of 1007 files, while the same check reading %an reports 980 -- indistinguishable from no check at all. Any tool comparing a file's recorded author names against git history must use %aN.

sapience_notes.subject: A .mailmap cannot express an excluded identity
sapience_notes.value: A .mailmap can rename and merge author identities but has no 'drop' form by construction, so an identity that should earn no attribution at all (an agent identity, a bot) cannot be handled there and needs a separate exclusion set in the consuming tool. Equally, %aN does not surface Co-Authored-By trailers, so an exclusion set can never be derived from %aN output alone -- it must be stated deliberately.

sapience_notes.subject: Attribution checks must report candidates, not verdicts
sapience_notes.value: git records who authored a commit, not whether that commit merged someone else's pull request or materially edited a file. A name-vs-history comparison therefore cannot produce a verdict. The workable design gates exit status on UNREVIEWED candidates against a stamped waiver baseline (row = path + identity + the file's current author line), so a reviewed-and-declined candidate goes green while any later header edit un-grandfathers the row and re-raises it.

sapience_notes.subject: An import-only-diff rule beats an enumerated exemption list
sapience_notes.value: Barrel/aggregator roots attract commits that only add or reorder imports. Exempting them by a rule -- a committer whose whole +/- footprint on a file is import and blank lines earns no attribution -- clears them without naming them and keeps clearing them as the tree changes. Measured on this repository: the rule cleared 3 of 4 barrel roots automatically; the fourth survived because of one non-import docstring line, which is the honest reason to waive it. The tempting grounds 'its body is just imports' was measured FALSE (27/73/79/297 non-import body lines).

sapience_notes.subject: A near-equal +/- line count is the signature of a mechanical rename sweep
sapience_notes.value: When judging whether a commit earns authorship credit on a file, a diff whose additions and deletions are nearly equal and whose changed lines differ only in one renamed identifier is a propagation sweep, not authorship. Confirmed by inspecting at -U2 that each apparently-new line has its identical deletion one line up, re-wrapped. On this repository 7 of 24 forward attribution candidates were exactly this and were waived.

sapience_notes.subject: A repo-local .claude/ rule can be untracked end to end
sapience_notes.value: Putting a convention into agent context via a repo-local rule file under .claude/rules/ plus a .syncprotect entry can leave BOTH halves untracked: in this repository /.claude is gitignored at .gitignore:107 and /.syncprotect at .gitignore:83. The route buys mid-dispatch context reach in one working copy and reaches no clone, no CI and no collaborator. Check both paths with git check-ignore before claiming any reach, and keep the durable record in tracked files.

sapience_notes.subject: A duplicated expected=N assertion carries more prose than the plan counts
sapience_notes.value: Adding a check to a verification aggregator that asserts its own check count required five edits, not the three or four a plan predicts: the invocation, the report line, expected=N, AND every prose occurrence of the spelled-out count -- which appeared in four separate places (a PURPOSE line, an exit-code-contract line, a user-facing echo, and an in-comment 'checks 8 to 10' range). Grep for the spelled-out number, not just the numeral.

sapience_notes.subject: Lean test libraries outside defaultTargets leave stale oleans after lake build
sapience_notes.value: In a Lake project where a test library declares srcDir = "Tests" and is absent from defaultTargets, a plain `lake build` reports complete success while every touched test module's .olean stays older than its source. Verifying a build covered the files you edited therefore needs a per-module .olean-newer-than-source check plus an explicit `lake build <TestLib>`, not just the success line and a zero error count.
